AcceptedEmails.description:
What `POST /v1/emails` accepted: the email, or one per address when `to`
held several.

AccountExport.description: The whole-account export: every row the account owns, by table.

data.description:
`account` holds the account itself; every other key names a table
and holds the account's rows in it, column by column. A column added
to a table later appears here without a new API version.

monthly_quota.description:
Emails this account may send this period. This is the ceiling actually
enforced, which is the free allowance until the first non-zero invoice
settles — it can therefore be lower than the plan's headline number.

AddedContacts.description:
What adding contacts did: the contact when one `email` was sent, the
counts when a `contacts` array was.

auto_responder_rules.description: The auto-responder rules, as last set with the auto-responder endpoint.

skip_spam_webhooks.description: Skip webhooks for messages judged spam; they are still stored.

AnalyticsSummary.description: Summary analytics for a given time period.

bounce_rate_pct.description: Bounced share of the same denominator as `delivery_rate_pct`.

click_rate_pct.description: Unique clicks per delivered send; `None` when nothing was delivered.

complaint_rate_pct.description: Complaints per delivered send; `None` when nothing was delivered.

delivery_rate_pct.description:
Share of the sends that reached an outcome (delivered, bounced or
failed) that were delivered. `None` when no send reached an outcome:
the rate is unknown, and 0% would claim every send failed.

open_rate_pct.description: Unique opens per delivered send; `None` when nothing was delivered.

total_clicks.description: Every recorded click event, including repeat clicks.

total_complaints.description: Spam complaints, one per complaining recipient.

total_failed.description:
Sends given up on after retries, on our side. Part of the denominator
of `delivery_rate_pct` and `bounce_rate_pct`, with delivered and bounced.

total_hard_bounces.description: Bounces the receiving server called permanent; part of `total_bounced`.

total_opens.description: Every recorded open event, including re-opens of the same email.

total_proxy_opens.description:
Open-pixel fetches made by a provider's image proxy or scanner. Not
part of `total_opens` or the open rate, and not people: a proxy fetches
on arrival and can fetch the same message again on later days.
Reported so a low open rate can be read for what it is.

total_rejected.description:
Sends stopped before any delivery attempt. Not part of any rate's
denominator: nothing was handed to a receiving server.

total_soft_bounces.description: Bounces the receiving server called temporary; part of `total_bounced`.

total_unique_clicks.description: Emails clicked at least once; the click-rate numerator.

total_unique_opens.description: Emails opened at least once; the open-rate numerator.

unsubscribe_rate_pct.description: Unsubscribes per delivered send; `None` when nothing was delivered.

ApiKeySummary.description: A key as listed. The secret is never shown after creation.

AttachmentDownload.description: One attachment of a message, with a download link when the file is held.

url.description: A pre-signed download URL. Absent when the file was not kept.

AttachmentMetadata.description: One attachment of a received message, as recorded when it arrived.

AutoResponder.description: A mailbox's auto-responder after the change.

emails.description: The emails to send, each shaped like the body of `POST /v1/emails`.

rate_limited.description:
The emails in `errors` that a send-rate limit or the new-account
allowance refused, with how long to wait. Retry these after the wait.

BatchRateLimited.description:
An email of a batch that a rate limit refused. Listed in `errors` as well;
this entry adds what a client needs to retry it.

retry_after_seconds.description: Seconds until the window that refused this email resets.

BatchRefusal.description:
A refused batch. Once the batch was processed, the per-email outcome; when
the request itself was refused first (an empty or oversized batch, the
account's request limit), the error body.

transactional.description:
Whether this is a transactional broadcast. Defaults to `false` because
bulk sends are typically marketing emails that need `List-Unsubscribe` headers
for Gmail/Yahoo compliance. Set to `true` only for operational bulk sends
(e.g. account migration notices) where unsubscribe headers are inappropriate.

inserted.description: Contacts added. Addresses already on the list are skipped.

CheckStatus.description: Pass/warn/fail status for a single DNS health check.

CheckoutSession.description: Where to send the customer to pay.

ContactListSummary.description: A contact list and how many contacts it holds.

skip_spam_webhooks.description: Skip the webhook for messages judged spam. Defaults to `false`.

display_name.description: Optional human-readable label for this mailbox.

domain_id.description:
Domain ID for a custom domain owned by this account.
The domain must have `inbound_enabled=true` and `mx_verified=true`.
If omitted, uses the platform domain (`inbound.euromail.dev`).

local_part.description: Custom local part (e.g. "toimitus"). If omitted, a random `mb-xxxx` is generated.

custom_fields.description: Custom fields rendered on the form.

description.description: Optional description shown below the title.

from_address.description:
From address for confirmation emails (e.g. noreply@yourdomain.com).
Must use a verified domain. Defaults to noreply@<first verified domain>.

list_id.description: Contact list ID to attach this form to.

redirect_url.description: URL to redirect to after subscription (overrides success_message).

theme.description:
Theme customization: bg_color, text_color, button_color, button_text_color,
border_color, accent_color, border_radius, font_family, embed, hide_branding.

preheader.description:
Inbox preview text shown after the subject. Rendered with
`template_data` and added as a hidden block at the top of the HTML
part. Omit or leave blank for none.

events.description:
Event types to receive: sent, deferred, bounced, failed, opened,
clicked, complained, email.inbound, mailbox.message.received,
account.auto_paused, insights.generated.

CreatedApiKey.description: A key just created. `key` is the secret, shown this once and never again.

key_prefix.description: The first characters of the key, shown in lists to tell keys apart.

warnings.description:
Present when the domain was accepted but something about it is worth
flagging; today, a name that already carries the sending subdomain.

CreatedWebhook.description:
A webhook just created. `secret` signs every delivery; it is shown this
once and never again.

DeadLetter.description: A message the delivery pipeline gave up on.

payload.description: The message as it was queued.

stream_id.description: The id to retry or delete it by.

DeadLetterList.description: The account's dead letters, newest first.

total.description: Dead letters the account has in all, of which `data` holds up to `count`.

scheduled_for.description:
When the data is erased. Until then `POST /v1/account/restore` calls
the deletion off.

subscription_still_running.description:
True when the paid subscription could not be cancelled and is still
billing; cancel it in the billing portal.

Deliverable.description:
Deliverability assessment: "yes" if MX records found, "no" if invalid syntax
or disposable, "unknown" if MX lookup failed or timed out.

alignment.description: Whether mail we send for this domain can pass the DMARC policy it publishes.

lookup_failed.description: The DNS lookup did not answer, so `verified` says nothing about the record.

DmarcSeverity.description: How loudly the domain page and API report the result.

detected_provider.description:
The DNS host detected for the domain (`cloudflare`, `other`, ...),
once a check has run. Defaulted so a pod that starts before the
migration adding the column has run can still read domains.

dns_checked_at.description:
Last time the DNS monitor attempted a check of this verified domain,
whether or not the lookups produced an answer.

dns_drift_detected_at.description:
When the monitor first saw a verified record stop matching. `None`
while the records match. Sending is not blocked while this is set.

dns_drift_records.description: Which records stopped matching: any of `spf`, `dkim`, `return_path`.

dns_records.description:
The DNS records to publish, keyed by purpose (`spf`, `dkim`, `dmarc`,
`return_path`, ...). Every value is a record; nothing else goes here.

DomainCheckResponse.description: The DNS health of a domain.

cached.description: True when the answer comes from the last ten minutes' cache.

detected_provider.description: The mail provider the MX records point at, when recognised.

DomainDmarcStatus.description: The customer-facing result for one domain.

adkim.description: `r` (relaxed) or `s` (strict) DKIM alignment mode of the policy.

can_pass.description: Whether DMARC can pass for mail from this domain.

dkim_domain.description: Domain our DKIM signature uses (`d=`); `null` when the domain has no key.

existing_record.description: The DMARC record as published, at `record_host`.

pct.description: Share of failing mail the policy applies to, 0-100.

policy.description: Policy applied to the domain: `none`, `quarantine` or `reject`; `null` without a DMARC record.

record_host.description:
DNS name of the DMARC record the policy comes from, which may be the
organizational domain's rather than the domain's own.

relax_tags.description: Tags to change to relaxed alignment (`adkim=r`, `aspf=r`); empty when relaxing would not help.

return_path_domain.description: Domain of the Return-Path SPF is checked against.

suggested_record.description:
The one record to publish at `record_host`: the existing record with
our report address added and, when mail is blocked, the strict tag
relaxed. `null` when nothing needs to change.

summary.description: One plain-language sentence; empty when `severity` is `ok`.

sending_ip.description: The source IP address used to deliver this email (set after SMTP delivery).

suppress_list_management_header.description: When true, omit List-Unsubscribe and List-Unsubscribe-Post headers

tracking_override.description: Per-email tracking override: None = use account default, Some(true) = force on, Some(false) = force off

transactional_declared.description:
The sender explicitly declared the send transactional; only such a
send reaches an address that unsubscribed.

dead_letters.description: Messages to the address the delivery pipeline gave up on.

operation_id.description: The operation that recorded the erasure.

EmailDataExport.description: Everything the account holds about one email address.

event_type.description:
One of `queued`, `processing`, `sent`, `delivered`, `bounced`,
`failed`, `rejected`, `deferred`, `opened`, `opened_proxy`, `clicked`,
`complained`, `unsubscribed`, and per CC/BCC recipient `cc_sent`,
`cc_deferred`, `cc_bounced`, `cc_failed`, `cc_rejected` and the `bcc_`
equivalents (the recipient is in `raw_payload`).
`opened_proxy` is a fetch of the tracking image by a mail provider's
proxy or scanner: it is not counted as an open and sends no webhook.

EmailSummary.description: Summary of emails sent to a specific address within an account.

EmailWithEvents.description: One email and every event recorded for it, oldest first.

ErrorBody.description: The body of every 4xx and 5xx response.

ErrorDetail.description:
What went wrong. `code` is the stable, machine-readable part; `message` is
for people and may change.

current.description: An action refused because the state changed: the state it found.

docs_url.description: A guide that explains how to fix it, when there is one.

suppressed_at.description:
`RECIPIENT_SUPPRESSED`: when the address was suppressed; null when
that is not recorded. Absent on other codes.

suspended_at.description:
`ACCOUNT_SUSPENDED`: when sending was paused; null when that is not
recorded. Absent on other codes.

ForPeriod_AnalyticsSummary.description: A result and the date range it covers.

ForPeriod_Vec_RecipientDomainStats.description: A result and the date range it covers.

ForPeriod_Vec_TagStat.description: A result and the date range it covers.

ForPeriod_Vec_TimeseriesPoint.description: A result and the date range it covers.

emails.description: List of email addresses to suppress.

spam_reasons.description: The evidence behind the verdict as stable codes, worst first.

spam_verdict.description:
`clean`, `suspect`, `spam`, or `unchecked` when no check could run;
null for messages received before verdicts were recorded.

skip_spam_webhooks.description: Skip webhooks for messages judged spam; they are still stored.

webhook_id.description: The webhook row carrying this route's URL, once it has one.

InsightReport.description: A written report on the account's recent sending.

findings.description: The findings behind the summary, each with what was seen and what to do.

summary.description: The headline, one or two sentences.

LeasedMessage.description:
A message leased to the caller. Acknowledge it with `lease_token` before
`lease_expires_at`, or it returns to the queue.

LinkClickStat.description: Per-link click statistics for a single email.

clicks.description: Total number of clicks recorded for this URL.

last_clicked_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent click.

unique_clicks.description: Number of distinct UTC calendar days on which this URL was clicked.

sent_messages.description: Messages sent from the mailbox (replies and new messages).

total_messages.description:
Messages received. Mail sent from the mailbox is counted in
`sent_messages`, not here, so the two never double-count a thread.

total_threads.description:
Conversations in either direction: a thread the mailbox opened and
nobody has answered yet counts, so this can exceed `total_messages`.

MailboxContact.description: Contact derived from mailbox message history.

display_name.description: Most recent display name seen for this email.

email.description: Normalized email address (lowercase, stripped from display name).

direction.description:
`inbound` for mail the mailbox received, `outbound` for mail sent from
it (a reply or a new message). Outbound rows are stored already read so
the lease queue never hands an agent its own outgoing mail.

email_id.description: The `emails` row the send pipeline created for an outbound row.

spam_verdict.description:
Spam verdict and its evidence, as on `InboundEmail`; null on
outbound rows and on messages received before verdicts were recorded.

spf_result.description:
Sender checks for a received message (`None` on outbound rows and on
messages received before they were recorded): SPF, DKIM and DMARC
verdicts, the forward-confirmed name of the sending server, the mail
service it belongs to, the HELO it announced, and the country of its IP.

to_addresses.description:
Bare, lower-cased recipients (To + Cc) of an outbound row; empty for
inbound rows.

MessageLabels.description: A message's labels after the change.

NewsletterList.description: One page of newsletters, newest first.

NewsletterWithStats.description: A newsletter, with its delivery stats once it has been sent.

OutboundMessage.description: A message sent from a mailbox, a reply or a new one.

mailbox_message_id.description:
The message as recorded in the mailbox's thread; null when it could
not be recorded (see `recorded`).

Pagination.description: Where a page sits in the whole list.

All data associated with a specific email address within an account.
`dead_letters` is added by the API handler, which reads them from Redis.

engagement.description: The address's engagement record (opens, clicks, last activity), if any.

fbl_reports.description: Spam complaints received about mail to the address, as stored.

webhook_deliveries.description: Webhook deliveries whose payload names the address, as stored.

The date range a result covers, both ends included. Each endpoint fills

ip_hold_started_at.description:

toward its provider; the hold window runs from here. Cleared when an

return_path_domain.description:
Domain of the copy's VERP return path; a DSN counts only if it came
back to this domain.

key (per account) returns the original email instead of creating a new one.

send_at.description: Time to send the email (ISO 8601). Omit to send immediately.

stream.description:
Message stream slug. Routes this email through the named stream, enabling
separate reputation tracking for transactional vs. marketing email.
Defaults to `"transactional"`. The stream must exist for the account.

subject.description: Subject line. Required unless `template_alias` supplies one.

tags.description: Labels for filtering and analytics.

template_alias.description: Alias of a stored template to render instead of `html_body` and `text_body`.

template_data.description: Variables passed to the template named by `template_alias`.

transactional.description:

the message to the Primary inbox instead of Promotions.

get.description:
Blocks until a new message is available or the timeout expires.

On success, acquires a lease on the oldest deliverable message. The lease
hides the message from other pollers until the agent calls `/ack` or
`/nack`, or until `lease_expires_at` passes (at which point the message
returns to the queue). Returns 408 on timeout.

Response body:
```json
{ "data": <message>, "lease_token": "uuid", "lease_expires_at": "..." }
```

408.description: No message arrived before the timeout (code NO_MESSAGE)

post.description: Send up to 500 emails in a single request. Returns an operation_id for tracking, a data array of queued emails, and an errors array for any per-email failures. Partial success is supported. An email refused by a send-rate limit or the new-account allowance is also listed in rate_limited with code RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED and retry_after_seconds. When no email was accepted and every refusal is such a limit, the response is 429 with a retry-after header set to the longest wait; the body is the same.

422.description: Validation error, or no email was accepted and not all refusals were rate limits

429.description: Every email was refused by a send-rate limit or the new-account allowance, or the account's request limit was hit. The retry-after header holds the longest wait.

delete.description:
Permanently deletes every table [`gdpr::GDPR_COVERED_TABLES`] names for the specified
email address — emails (as the envelope recipient), events, tracking tokens,
CC/BCC deliveries to the address,
suppressions, unsubscribe events, contacts, inbound emails, agent mailbox messages,
engagement stats, webhook delivery logs and ISP feedback-loop reports — plus matching
entries in the Redis dead letter queue. An email where the address appears only as a
cc, bcc or reply-to is redacted (the address is stripped from those fields) rather than
deleted, since deleting it would destroy a different recipient's delivery record. Logs
the action in the audit trail, storing a masked form of the address rather than the
plaintext. Rate limited to 1 request per
minute per account.
